unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 12-LEVEL: B1.4 THEME 6: LIFE IN THE UNIVERSE & FUTURE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will explore the theme ''Life in the Universe and the Future'' by investigating topics such as space organisations; and plans and aspirations for the future. They will research advancements made by global space organisations and examine their ambitious missions to explore space and understand our universe. Students will also envision their own plans and aspirations for the future, either on a personal level or as part of humanity’s collective progress in space exploration and technology. The assignment can take the form of a creative presentation, a futuristic essay, or a visual project imagining life on another planet, encouraging students to think critically about humanity's place in the universe and the role of innovation in shaping the future. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the universe and the future with its components such as space organisations; plans and aspirations for the future'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 12 may know what space organisations; plans and aspirations for the future mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 12 they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the universe and the future'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''to design, to predict, smart homes, virtual reality, and so on'' and also some structures such as ''If scientists work much more carefully, they can discover the signs of life on Mars. If he worked on a project, he would plan to study on manned space missions'' in English from the previous themes or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year, and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''life in the universe and the future with its components such as space organisations; plans and aspirations for the future'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To write a paragraph about space exploration and aspirations for the future in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Complete the Paragraph The teacher prepares a partially written paragraph about space exploration and the future. Students work in groups of 3-4 for a collaborative activity. Each group brainstorms ideas to complete the paragraph using the target vocabulary, such as ''space agency'', ''determined'', and ''to achieve success'', providing a logical flow and creative contributions. After writing 4-5 sentences to complete the paragraph, one group member reads their work aloud to the class. The teacher and classmates provide constructive feedback, focusing on the effective use of target vocabulary, target grammar, and creativity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Partially Written Paragraph: ''Space exploration has always been a source of inspiration for humanity. International organisations work constantly on innovative missions to uncover the mysteries of the universe. While some problems occur, scientists and astronauts try to push the boundaries of what is possible. In the future, ...''.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe space organisations and aspirations for the future in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Exploring Space and Dreaming Big The teacher prepares a paragraph and explains the activity to the students. First, students read the paragraph carefully. While reading, they underline the words related to space organisations (e.g., space mission, satellite) and aspirations for the future (e.g., set goals, achieve success). Second, they find one sentence in the paragraph that uses a modal verb in the past (e.g., could have stopped space research). After identifying it, write a simple explanation of its meaning. For example, this means they had the ability to stop research, but they didn’t. Third, they write one sentence about their own goal for the future. They use expressions like ''to achieve success'' or ''to set goals''. For example, ''I set goals to become a scientist in the future''. Then the teacher listens and gives feedback on pronunciation and sentence correctness. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Activity Text: ''…. is a famous space agency that works on space missions and launches rockets to explore space. In the past, they could have stopped space research, but they didn’t. Instead, they collected samples from space and used satellites to study the universe. Now, many people set goals to become astronauts and work on space stations. Some students are determined to achieve success and accomplish their dreams. If they make progress, their dreams of exploring space will come true one day''.
